reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Audit a game's player-facing access paths across communication, controls, motion, visual distinction, text presentation, difficulty, and interruption handling.
neutralIntentExamples: audit a game for accessible communication, controls, motion, visual distinction, and text presentation
design an accessibility test pass covering desaturation, muting, one-handed play, zoom, and effect toggles
inputs: gameplay, interface, audio, visual-effect, and difficulty requirements
operations: identify information and interaction barriers
specify adjustable alternatives and defaults
exercise the game under reduced sensory and motor conditions
record unresolved access failures before release
failureBehavior: retain release readiness as unverified when accessibility cases have not been exercised
escalate safety-critical flashing or unreadable interaction rather than masking it with a claim of compliance
exclusions: treating accessibility as optional polish
assuming one accommodation covers every disability or platform
making legal or store-compliance claims without current verification
usefulInvariants: critical information has non-color channels
controls and presentation can be adjusted without removing core play
reduced-effect modes remain playable and legible
human testing supplements automated checks
materialRisks: numeric thresholds and legal duties vary by platform and jurisdiction
accessibility controls can create inconsistent game states if not tested together
a checklist can miss barriers specific to a game's mechanic or hardware

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Plan a compact game-audio system spanning generated effects, recorded assets, playback limits, gesture-gated startup, event mixing, silence, and attribution.
neutralIntentExamples: plan a mobile game audio stack for generated effects, music, playback limits, and mute persistence
audit game sound design for variation, impact layering, first-gesture startup, and recorded-asset attribution
inputs: sound-event inventory and available generated or recorded assets
operations: select an audio generation and playback approach
define variation, layering, voice limits, and event ducking
handle user-gesture initialization and mute state
measure payload and verify behavior on representative mobile hardware
record licenses and attribution for non-generated audio
failureBehavior: leave audio readiness unresolved when device startup or licensing evidence is absent
degrade or suppress repeated voices rather than allowing clipping and thread overload
exclusions: assuming a free download has a safe commercial license
treating audio presence as evidence of audio quality
starting playback before the platform permits it
usefulInvariants: repeated events are perceptually varied
concurrent playback is bounded
mute behavior is persistent and platform-aware
impact feedback and silence remain coordinated
materialRisks: browser and device audio policies differ
procedural sound parameters still require tuning and review
third-party asset and library terms may change or conflict with distribution

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Tune immediate game response through prioritized visual, temporal, audio, camera, motion, input-forgiveness, and haptic feedback with a short observational test.
neutralIntentExamples: prioritize feedback changes that make a mechanically correct game clearer and more responsive
test whether impacts remain legible in a short gameplay recording with audio disabled
inputs: recorded gameplay and target-device interaction constraints
operations: rank feedback interventions by player value
add or tune impact, motion, camera, input-window, and haptic responses
bound effect duration and intensity
inspect silent footage for readable impacts
outputs: observable feel issues and measured follow-up questions
failureBehavior: keep feel claims provisional when only code inspection is available
reduce or remove feedback that reads as lag, noise, or nausea
exclusions: equating more effects with better feel
treating example timing values as universal
using polish to conceal unclear mechanics
usefulInvariants: feedback is tied to a player-relevant event
high-value response is addressed before decorative effects
effect intensity and duration are bounded
human observation remains the acceptance gate
materialRisks: feel is genre- and action-dependent
stacked feedback can conflict with accessibility settings
short clips may not expose fatigue or repetition problems

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Choose and govern authored or procedural character motion based on silhouette variability, then specify readable layering, transitions, interruption, and verification rules.
neutralIntentExamples: choose an animation strategy for fixed and configurable character silhouettes
define input buffering, cancellation, interruption, and reaction rules for character actions
inputs: action list, movement rules, and responsiveness requirements
operations: classify subjects by whether their silhouette can vary
select authored, procedural, or mixed motion
add secondary motion, look-at, ground adaptation, and additive layers as justified
define buffering, cancellation, and reaction interruption per action
verify motion readability and transitions
failureBehavior: mark responsiveness unverified when action interruption rules are undocumented or untested
treat hard transitions, floating, and dropped input as defects requiring design review
exclusions: assuming procedural motion is cheaper for every body
locking input as an accidental animation side effect
judging beauty before legibility
usefulInvariants: the animation approach follows subject variability
movement and defense interruption is deliberate
reaction control loss is an explicit design cost
motion communicates state before ornament
materialRisks: procedural locomotion has high tuning cost
buffer and cancel windows can alter balance
mixed authored and procedural systems need consistent transition ownership

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Treat model-assisted game art as a production pipeline with generation, cleanup, palette and material coherence, derived maps, silhouette checks, and licensing gates.
neutralIntentExamples: design a game-art generation pipeline that preserves palette, silhouette, material, and asset provenance
evaluate whether generated art is suitable for a coherent playable set rather than a single attractive image
inputs: art direction, target resolution, and asset roles
generator terms, model terms, and required texture or material outputs
operations: generate candidate assets
remove matte and background artifacts
normalize palette and visual register
derive normal or height information where needed
run silhouette and consistency checks
record model and output rights
failureBehavior: withhold release use when output rights or coherence evidence is unresolved
fall back to authored or conventional assets where generation cannot meet consistency requirements
exclusions: assuming a model license grants unrestricted output rights
shipping raw generations as finished production art
using generated characters when frame-to-frame consistency is unproven
usefulInvariants: palette and silhouette remain coherent across assets
generation is only one stage of production
rights are recorded for the exact tool and output path
readability is tested at target size
materialRisks: generator and model terms can restrict commercial output
cleanup and coherence work may exceed the presumed time saving
derived maps can introduce shading artifacts

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Assess an on-device generative character feature across model, runtime, training provenance, ratings, grounding, latency, hardware, saves, adversarial behavior, and offline fallback.
neutralIntentExamples: audit an on-device game character feature for licenses, ratings, grounding, latency, privacy, and fallback behavior
design a constrained local dialogue system that can only use revealed game state and stores its transcript
inputs: model weights, runtime version, and provenance records
revealed game state, content policy, target devices, and distribution requirements
operations: audit all relevant licenses and provenance
check ratings and disclosure requirements
constrain generation and filter output
measure size and latency on the hardware floor
test unrevealed-information leakage and jailbreaks
store transcript state and verify an authored silent fallback
outputs: adversarial, performance, provenance, and offline-fallback evidence
failureBehavior: defer release when any rights, ratings, leakage, or hardware gate is unresolved
prefer authored selection or silence over unsafe or generic free generation
exclusions: treating a prompt as a security boundary
assuming a model card is the complete license
making privacy or ratings claims without tests and written platform evidence
usefulInvariants: the model sees only revealed state
the feature remains bounded and filterable
the character has value without the model
generated transcript is persisted as state rather than reconstructed from a seed
materialRisks: weights, runtime, and training provenance can impose separate restrictions
local output cannot be patched server-side after release
size and latency may exclude lower-end devices
adversarial users can expose content and plot leaks

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Design game visual effects as bounded feedback, prioritizing impact readability, temporal response, trauma-based camera motion, controlled particles, persistent decals, shaders, and device-aware budgets.
neutralIntentExamples: prioritize game visual feedback for impacts before adding decorative particle volume
design a device-aware effect budget with pooled particles, bounded shake, persistent decals, and measurable draw cost
inputs: game events and intended player interpretations
rendering engine capabilities and target-device performance budget
operations: map effects to feedback questions
implement or tune flash, stop, shake, particles, decals, and shaders
pool and cap transient resources
adapt budgets to device class
measure effect cost at representative entity counts
outputs: readability, accessibility, licensing, and performance evidence
failureBehavior: defer decorative effects when core feedback is unreadable or performance is unmeasured
remove or scale effects that cause nausea, noise, or frame-time failure
exclusions: using particles as a substitute for clear hit feedback
adding a second emitter library when the engine already supplies one
assuming shader or helper-library licensing is safe without inspection
usefulInvariants: each effect communicates a player-relevant event
transient resources are pooled and globally bounded
motion reduction remains available
performance is measured on target-like hardware
materialRisks: effect stacking can overwhelm players and accessibility settings
persistent render targets consume memory and complicate lifecycle
mobile GPU and allocation behavior differ from desktop
gore and color treatment affect rating and tone

reviews.neutralCapabilitySummary: Establish a coherent game-art baseline from a controlled source and palette, readable silhouettes, licensed assets, generated-art limits, and atlas-aware delivery.
neutralIntentExamples: establish a coherent game-art baseline with one palette, readable silhouettes, and recorded asset licenses
prepare shippable placeholder art at final size and verify atlas packing and draw-call impact
inputs: game art direction and target display size
candidate asset sources, licenses, palette, and rendering constraints
operations: select and document a primary asset source
define and enforce a shared palette
build final-size placeholders
test silhouettes and faction readability
record licenses and attribution
pack atlases and count draw calls
failureBehavior: defer asset use when license or attribution status is unresolved
replace or recolor mismatched assets rather than allowing visual incoherence to accumulate
exclusions: optimizing for isolated asset quality over set coherence
bulk-downloading assets without per-file license review
assuming generated art is reliable for consistent animated characters
usefulInvariants: palette and source discipline are explicit
player, enemy, pickup, and hazard silhouettes remain distinguishable at target size
placeholder art is tested at production scale
atlas and draw-call costs are observable
materialRisks: asset licenses and attribution requirements vary by file
palette restrictions can conflict with accessibility contrast needs
atlas packing can complicate streaming and layer ownership
generated backgrounds or key art may have separate commercial-rights questions
